locators: p. 2, Purpose of Form, "File Form 1116 to claim the foreign tax credit if the election, earlier, doesn’t apply and", "You paid or accrued certain foreign taxes to a foreign country or U.S. territory"; p. 1, "This election is available only if you meet all of the following conditions"
pp. 1–2, election to claim the foreign tax credit without filing Form 1116; p. 25, Line 20, regular tax

findings.who: A filer whose only foreign tax was passed through on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) from an estate or trust, or on a Schedule K-3 (Form 1065 or 1120-S) from a partnership or S corporation. They received no Form 1099-INT with box 6 or Form 1099-DIV with box 7.
findings.why_no: The helper says 'generally Form 1099-INT box 6 and Form 1099-DIV box 7'. If it is filled from those boxes, or the filer reads it as limited to them, it computes $0, so the condition is false.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 1: 'Qualified payee statements include Form 1099-DIV, Form 1099-INT, Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), Schedule K-3 (Form 1065), Schedule K-3 (Form 1120-S), or similar substitute statements.'
findings.fix: Add K-1 (1041) and K-3 (1065/1120-S) foreign taxes to the helper. Ask 'Did you or your spouse have foreign tax shown on any 1099, K-1, K-3, or substitute statement?' and ask for each amount.

findings.who: A filer, or the spouse on a joint return, who paid foreign income tax directly or had it withheld with no payee statement. Examples: tax withheld on foreign wages not excluded, on a foreign pension or foreign rent, or tax paid to a foreign province or a U.S. territory.
findings.why_no: No 1099 box 6 or box 7 amount exists, so a helper built from those boxes, or a filer following the 'generally' list, gives $0.
findings.line: ftc.eligible_if_tax (Form 1116 path); all gated lines become false
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 2: 'File Form 1116 to claim the foreign tax credit if the election, earlier, doesn't apply and ... You paid or accrued certain foreign taxes to a foreign country or U.S. territory.'
findings.fix: Make the gate a fact the filer can check: 'Did you or your spouse pay, or have withheld, any income tax to a foreign country, a foreign city or province, or a U.S. territory, on any income?' Then collect the amounts by source, not only from 1099 boxes.

findings.who: A filer with a foreign tax carryover from an earlier year (shown on Schedule B (Form 1116)) and foreign-source income this year, but no foreign tax paid or accrued this year.
findings.why_no: This year's creditable foreign taxes are truly $0, so the condition is false and the tool treats Form 1116 as not applying.
findings.line: ftc.eligible_if_tax (Form 1116 path, carryover absorbed on line 10); ftc.elect_if_tax
findings.irs_text: i1116 pp. 1-2: 'You can't carry over to or from any other year any foreign taxes paid or accrued in a tax year to which the election applies (but carryovers to and from other years are unaffected). See the instructions for line 10'; p. 2: 'Use Schedule B (Form 1116) to reconcile your prior-year foreign tax carryover with your current-year foreign tax carryover.'
findings.fix: Widen the gate: foreign taxes this year > 0 OR a foreign tax carryover from a prior year > 0. Ask 'Do you have an unused foreign tax credit carryover from an earlier year (prior Form 1116 / Schedule B)?'

findings.who: A filer with no new foreign tax this year who had a foreign tax redetermination for a prior year, such as an additional assessment or a refund, that must be reported.
findings.why_no: The helper counts this year's creditable foreign taxes, so the filer enters $0 and the redetermination is never reached.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 2: 'Use Schedule C (Form 1116) to report foreign tax redeterminations that occurred in the current tax year and that relate to prior tax years.'
findings.fix: Add to the gate: 'Did you or your spouse pay additional foreign tax, or receive a refund of foreign tax, this year for an earlier year?' Route a yes to Schedule C (Form 1116).

findings.who: A filer with foreign tax withheld on dividends who is unsure whether the tax is 'creditable' or 'after required reductions', for example because of a holding period they cannot evaluate.
findings.why_no: The helper asks for 'creditable foreign taxes after required reductions', a legal classification. An unsure filer enters 0 rather than the box 7 amount.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 2: 'You are still required to take into account the general rules for determining whether a tax is creditable ... You are still required to reduce the taxes available for credit by any amount you would have entered on line 12 of Form 1116.'
findings.fix: Gate on gross foreign tax shown or paid (> $0). Apply creditability, holding-period, and line 12 reductions afterward through the ftc.eligible question.
